Tendencies: double-Protects leads vs Fake Out; reactive Protects on predicted big hits — Zard Protected into a double attack again this series, plan to pivot on those turns instead of attacking; Fake Outs the faster threat, will even Fake Out the Gengar slot despite Ghost immunity; Protects to stall weather; when down in the series benches Venusaur/Sinistcha for aggressive Fake Out + sun spam (Zard/Krook/Hydreigon/Sableye). Verified: Venusaur LO Earth Power 91-134% to Gengar — never stay in; Krook Crunch 93-133% to Mega Gengar; -1 Incin sun Flare Blitz 93.6-170% to Venusaur; Gleam 59.8-107.8% to Hydreigon; Hydreigon EB Dark Pulse 76-161% to Gengar but Gengar guaranteed faster; Gengar outspeeds Zard; Hurricane OHKOs LO Venusaur; Zard-Y sun Heat Wave only 21-29% to Garganacl and Solar Beam confirmed non-OHKO from full (~88%); Garganacl Salt Cure (prefer for accuracy) and Stone Edge both guaranteed-KO Zard-Y from 55%, Salt Cure confirmed KO at 26%; -2 Noivern Draco 18-32% to Zard-Y; Garganacl outlasts Hydreigon 1v1; Gleam confirmed KO on Sableye from 43%; Zard-Y sun Fire Blast 87-150% to Mega Gengar, Heat Wave does not OHKO Gengar. Endgame plan: Garganacl + Incineroar wall/close vs Zard; Gengar revenges slower targets; never stay in on Venusaur; Tailwind Noivern lead neutralizes Scarf Krook vs Mega Gengar. T

reflections.summary: The brought four (Charizard-Y, Krookodile, Hydreigon, Sableye) were critically weak to the opponent's Gengar + Noivern core. Three Dark types shared a Fairy weakness, letting Gengar’s Dazzling Gleam spread for massive damage. Noivern’s Tailwind gave the opponent permanent speed control, and Garganacl’s Wide Guard blocked Charizard’s Heat Wave and Krookodile’s Earthquake. Charizard-Y was the only Fairy-resistant Pokémon and was quickly overwhelmed by Stone Edge and fast special attacks.
reflections.adjustment: Replace the Dark-heavy backline with a Fairy-resistant Pokémon (e.g., a Steel type) and a speed-control option (e.g., Trick Room or a fast Taunt). Lead Charizard-Y alongside a Steel type to pressure Gengar and Noivern, while reversing the speed advantage. Avoid bringing multiple Dark-weak Pokémon into this opponent’s core.
reflections.notebook: Garganacl Stone Edge OHKOs Charizard-Y; must be eliminated before it moves. Noivern Focus Sash confirmed intact at 18%—only activates from full. Opponent consistently leads Gengar + Noivern; Gengar often Protects turn 1 while Noivern sets Tailwind. Gengar’s Dazzling Gleam threatens all Dark types; avoid stacking Dark-weak Pokémon. Garganacl’s Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave and Earthquake. Opponent’s preferred four is Incineroar/Garganacl/Noivern/Gengar; they rely on speed control and Fairy spread. Counter with a Fairy-resistant sweeper and a way to negate Tailwind (e.g., Trick Room, fast Taunt, or your own Tailwind). Incineroar is the fourth but rarely seen; likely brought for Intimidate/Fake Out support.
